Subject: Post-call: on-prem reserved capacity scope + next steps

Hi Samantha / Gabe —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next steps so everyone is aligned: 

Key pain points you shared:
- Unpredictable tail latency during concurrent inference peaks (impacting sync API endpoints)
- Strict data isolation requirements for model inputs and audit logs (security team)
- Need to keep per-token costs predictable for budgeting the next 12 months

Your high-level goals: 
- Move to an on-prem / private deployment with reserved GPU capacity (isolation from multi-tenant workloads)
- Achieve stable p95 latency targets for typical inference (target: < 250ms for 512-token requests)
- SLA level: target 99.9% uptime for inference endpoint; RTO/RPO discussion in SOW
- Procurement target: finalize commercial terms and PO within 4–6 weeks if sizing/price meet expectations

Our recommended starting configuration (subject to workbook validation):
- Dedicated pool: 4 x H100-equivalent GPUs for primary capacity, burst to 8 for peak windows
- Private control plane in your VPC with KMS-backed encryption and audit logs forwarded to your SIEM
- KV cache retention: per-tenant in-memory cache with optional persisted snapshots (configurable retention window)

Attached: redwood-capacity-workbook-v1.xlsx (capacity assumptions + cost model) and a preliminary pricing worksheet.

Next steps / asks: 
1) Please confirm the expected steady-state QPS and peak concurrency we should use for final sizing (I used the numbers you mentioned on call: steady 60 rps, peaks 220 concurrent requests).
2) Can your procurement contact be looped in? Procurement asked for SOC 2 and standard PO terms — procurement@helixai.com was mentioned.
3) We’ll prepare a short SOW draft + delivery timeline and share by EOD Wednesday next week (11/04).
4) Schedule: proposed technical deep-dive with Karthik and your infra team — Wed 11/04 11:00 AM ET (let me know if that works).

If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update the workbook. Thanks — excited to get this scoped.

Best,
Olga

Hi Samantha — quick responses to the compliance/architecture items you flagged, plus what we’ll bring to the Wed deep-dive: 

Encryption and KV cache
- KV cache: by default we keep KV in-memory for performance (no disk persistence). We offer optional persisted snapshots that are encrypted at rest if you choose snapshotting for warm restarts.
- Encryption: all data at rest (snapshots, logs) is encrypted using your KMS (customer-managed key via our KMS integration). TLS 1.3 for in-flight.

Isolation and on-prem model residency
- Private deployment options give you a single-tenant inference pool with no neighbor VM sharing. Control plane components can be run inside your VPC; data plane stays in your private network.

SLA / latency guarantees
- We can commit to operational SLO targets in the SOW (99.9% availability for the reserved pool). Latency SLOs are workload-dependent; for the model profile discussed we expect p95 < 250ms with the proposed hardware + reserved pool. We’ll include fallback routing and warm cache strategies in the runbook to avoid long tail spikes.

Attachments in this message: redwood-sow-draft-helixai.docx (initial SOW + milestones), pricing-worksheet-helixai.pdf (detailed PRICING / commitment tiers).

What I’ll bring to Wed: a deployment topology diagram, suggested autoscale/burst policy, and a short checklist for procurement items (SOC 2 report, network IP allowlist, PO template).

If procurement wants an initial quote to start paperwork we can provide a 30-day provisional quote based on the workbook numbers — let us know billing contact and PO terms.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.
Karthik
